subject: Post-call: inference evaluation — dedicated vs hyperscaler next steps
messages:
From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
To: Jonathan Park <jonathan.park@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-12-05T14:02:00-08:00
Subject: Post-call: inference evaluation — dedicated vs hyperscaler next steps

Thanks for the call earlier, Jonathan — really helpful to see Acme's prioritized evaluation criteria. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have a shared plan.

Recap (high level)
- Goal: Decide whether to lean on a Redwood Dedicated reservation or to architect against hyperscaler reserved/spot mix for production inference.
- Top evaluation priorities you called out: 99th-pt latency under peak, predictable reserved capacity, cold-start/KV-cache warmup impact, and clear unit-cost deltas across workloads.
- Models in scope: customer LLMs + open 70B variant for parity testing (you confirmed details below).

Proposed test matrix (we will lay out exact inputs/code in the sheet):
- P1: 99th-pt latency profile at target p99 SLA under steady-state and spike scenarios (150 TPS sustained, 300 TPS burst).
- P2: Failover and cross-region fallback behavior with <500ms added tail latency target.
- P3: Warm-cache vs cold-cache token delta (KV cache priming experiments).
- P4: Cost per 1k tokens measured across: Dedicated reserved, hyperscaler reserved instances, and hyperscaler preemptible/spot + autoscale.
- P5: Quantized model parity — output-quality checks for int8/4-bit variants where applicable.

Asks / actions for Acme (please):
1) Confirm the exact model versions you want us to test (we heard: Llama3-70B-int8 and a custom fine-tuned 16B).
2) Confirm target region (you mentioned US-West-2 as preferred).
3) Provide a contact in procurement to discuss reservation commitment language and cost floor (we'll send a short term-sheet).
4) Share any representative prompt set or a small anonymized sample payload set for token-size distribution.

We attached a short Mutual Action Plan (stub: acme-mrp-ma-plan.xlsx) and we'll populate the test matrix and test harness access by EOD tomorrow. Proposed bench week: Dec 14–18 (open to adjust).

If that aligns, I'll follow up with a single calendar invite and the Drive link to the test harness and runbook.

Thanks again — looking forward to validating tradeoffs and making the capacity decision concrete.

Best,
Irene Choi
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

+1 (415) 555-0192

Date: 2026-12-05T16:37:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: inference evaluation — dedicated vs hyperscaler next steps

Thanks, Irene — this is great and aligns with what we discussed. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Models: please run Llama3-70B (we'll accept int8) and our internal fine-tuned 16B (we'll supply a container or weights). Also please include a 8k vs 32k context-length profile.
- Traffic profile: Our internal QA will emulate two workloads — (A) steady inference at ~150 TPS with short responses (avg 120 tokens), (B) bursty interactive traffic with concurrency spikes to 400 TPS for ~10s every ~5m. The concurrency model is request-level (no stream) for test P1.
- SLA language: we need to understand what Redwood can guarantee for reserved capacity in a single region vs cross-region. Can Redwood commit to an isolation reservation (no noisy neighbor) or is it a best-effort throughput guarantee? Also what's the remediation path for missed p99 targets?
- Procurement: looped in procurement@acmehealth.com — they'll want a short-term commitment option (3–6 months) to start with, with credits if performance targets aren't met.

Attaching the draft SOW and an anonymized sample prompt set (we'll upload samples to the Drive link you provide).

Jonathan
Jonathan Park
Head of AI Engineering, Acme Health

Subject: RE: Post-call: inference evaluation — dedicated vs hyperscaler next steps

Looping in follow-ups and proposing concrete test scenarios we can run with minimal setup: 

Short plan (internal test ops)
- We will pre-provision: 3 Dedicated pools (small, medium, large) in us-west-2 mirroring expected reserved sizes + equivalent hyperscaler reserved/spot combos.
- Test harness: drive load from our bench infra, drive token distributions from Acme samples.
- P99 measurement: capture both request-level p99 and per-token latency; include tail percentiles at 99.9 for spike windows.
- Failure/fallback: simulate region outage and confirm cross-region cold-start adds <500ms per request (we'll define the tolerance).

Attachments: test-matrix.csv (schema for inputs, concurrency, durations). I'll also create a Drive folder with the runbook: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3cAcmeTestHarness

Timeline: target bench week Dec 14–18. Ops asks for Acme: provide the fine-tuned weights (or container) by Dec 10 and a procurement contact by Dec 8 so we can spin reserved capacity ahead of the run.

If no objections, I'll create infra reservations and post the concrete run schedule tomorrow.

- Sean
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference
